event_name: NAPA Auto Parts NHRA Midwest Nationals

pairs.note:
Weather conditions: air temperature 62 degrees, relative humidity 70 percent, barometer 30.19 inches, adjusted
altitude 756 feet, track temperature 82 degrees.

Josh Hart is 8-8 in Round 1 this year and 52-58 in his career. Tony Stewart beat Hart in Round 1 at Brainerd.

Stewart is 4 - 3 against Hart in prior events. 

Stewart with the starting line advantage, then was up in smoke right at the hit.  He pedaled and got it to
hook up enough to get the win.  the car did backfire on the top end.

Hart was up in smoke right at the hit and pedaled it, but was back up in smoke.

Spencer Massey “leaves first” 82% of the time in Round 1. Jasmine Salinas is 11-19 in Round 1 in her career.

This is the first time Massey and Salinas have faced each other in eliminations. 

Salinas with a slight starting line advantage and never trailed for the win.  She makes her quickest pass of
the season and her career fastest pass for the win.

Massey is up in smoke early and clicked it off.

Maddi Gordon is 11-5 in Round 1 this year. In both of his races against Gordon, Will Smith “left first.”

Gordon and Smith have each won 1 times against the other in prior events. 

Smith with the starting line advantage and never trailed for the win.  He makes his quickest and fastest pass
of the weekend for the win.  He will have lane choice over Stewart in the next round.

Antron Brown wins 80% of his Round 1 races when starting from the top half of the field. Clay Millican is 6-19
(24%) against Brown in Round 1.

Brown is 37 - 9 against Millican in prior events. 

Brown with the starting line advantage and never trailed for the win.

Millican is up in smoke right at the hit and clicked it off.

Shawn Langdon’s 416 round wins in TF are the 9th-most in class history. The No. 16 TF qualifier has never won
a round at this event.

Schumacher is 22 - 19 against Langdon in prior events. 

Langdon with the starting line advantage and never trailed for the win. He makes the quickest pass of race day
for the win.   He has a big top end speed to set the track speed record.  Shawn Langdon's incremental times:
60ft-0.831 sec., 330ft-2.111, 660ft-2.971/297.48 mph.

Schumacher with a good pass early but then pushes out a head gasket just past half track, but stayed with for
his quickest pass of the weekend in the losing effort.

Billy Torrence starts the event in 6th place, his highest starting position of the year. Justin Ashley starts
the event in 11th, marking the first time he has been outside the Top 10 since Gainesville in 2024.

Ashley with the starting line advantage and the power to hold on for the hole shot win. Justin Ashley's MOV:
0.0033 seconds (approximately 20 inches).  He will give up lane choice to Salinas in the next round.

Torrence with his quickest and fastest pass in the losing effort.

Shawn Reed has never “left first” against Kalitta. Doug Kalitta already has 41 round wins this year, his most
since 2016.

Kalitta is 6 - 3 against Reed in prior events. 

Kalitta with the starting line advantage, but is up in smoke early.

Reed kept it hooked up and hitting on all eight with his quickest and fastest pass for the win.  He will have
lane choice over Brown in the next round.

Leah Pruett is 9-8 in Round 1 when starting No. 8. The No. 8 TF qualifier is 9-5 in Round 1 at this event.
This is Kyle Wurtzel’s 38th start; his first came at this race in 2014.

Pruett is 3 - 0 against Wurtzel in prior events. 

Pruett with the starting line advantage and the power to hold on for the hole shot win.  She will give up lane
choice to Langdon in the next round
